summary: This document is a research discussion report (N3) arguing that methylene blue's (MB) working-memory (WM) benefit is not explained by MAO-A inhibition. It synthesizes existing literature on MB's redox and MAO-A mechanisms, identifies a critical gap (no same-task WM dissociation assay exists), and proposes a pre-registered rodent WM experiment to test the claim. The document is classified as a negative/assumption-kill discussion, not a completed experimental study.

content_blocks.content: Swarm ID: N3. Status: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative). Lane: nootropics. Risk class: research-discussion. Novelty: assumption-kill. Method: propose-assay. OpenLabs target: discussion (PASS_NEGATIVE — not claim). Mol Labs: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Cheap-IP: kill_cost_tier=1, time_to_refute=4 weeks, ip_class=redox-vs-MAO, vault_hold=no.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim
content_blocks.content: Methylene blue's working-memory benefit is NOT explained by MAO-A inhibition. The claim is operationalized as: (1) a redox-disabled MB analogue that retains MAO-A potency fails to match parent MB on a pre-registered rodent WM task (WM Δ ≤50% of parent or outside a pre-registered parent-equivalence band), AND (2) a selective MAO-A inhibitor at matched MAO occupancy does not reproduce parent MB WM within that same band.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: MB accepts electrons from NADH and feeds cytochrome c (mitochondrial redox cycling). N-acetyl / 10-N-impaired analogues lose mitochondrial complex activity and protective potency. Separately, MB is a tight-binding reversible MAO-A inhibitor (~70 nM) and Azure B is stronger (~11 nM), explaining serotonin-toxicity risk with SSRIs. Low-dose MB memory work maps to cytochrome oxidase (COX) / metabolic enhancement, not MAO panels. The document argues MAO potency and WM pharmacodynamics are different endpoint families until a dissociation assay exists.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: MB improves working memory because it inhibits MAO-A (same axis as serotonin toxicity / Azure B potency).

Baseline measured (literature):
- Redox-disabled N-acetyl-MB loses mitochondrial ET/complex activity (PMID 21454572; Wen 2011) — endpoint is mitochondrial/neuroprotection, NOT working memory.
- 10-N SAR: ~1000× drop in protective potency (PMID 23118969; Poteet 2012).
- MB increases COX and discrimination/metabolic-memory rescue (PMID 17428524; 21087672; Gonzalez-Lima class).
- MB MAO-A IC50 ≈70 nM; Azure B MAO-A IC50 ≈11 nM (PMID 17721552; 22197611).
- Paired WM ∩ MAO ∩ redox dissociation panel: UNKNOWN (does not exist).
- ≤50% parent-equivalence fail: PREDICTION (not yet tested).

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Endpoint mismatch: Wen (2011) redox-dead kill is mitochondrial/neuroprotection, not working memory; WM bridge is Gonzalez-Lima inference only.
2. Two live mechanisms (MAO-A and redox/COX) without a same-task dissociation for WM.
3. Azure B metabolite confound: in vivo 'MB' WM could still be metabolite-MAO even if parent redox matters in vitro.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature References
content_blocks.content:
- PMID 21454572 / DOI 10.1074/jbc.M110.208447 / PMC3091255 — Wen 2011: MB alternative electron transfer; N-acetyl redox-dead loses mitochondrial complex activity (neuroprotection/OCR endpoint — NOT WM).
- PMID 23118969 / DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0048279 / PMC3485214 — Poteet 2012: 10-N side-chain substitution → ~1000× drop in protective potency; redox SAR.
- PMID 17428524 / PMC2040387; PMID 21087672 / PMC3026638 — Gonzalez-Lima class: low-dose MB improves discrimination learning / rescues PCC-metabolic amnesia with COX upregulation.
- PMID 17721552 / PMC2078225; PMID 22197611 — Ramsay; Petzer: MB potent MAO-A inhibitor; Azure B MAO-A IC50 ≈11 nM vs MB ≈70 nM.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design (Ablation Logic)
content_blocks.content:
Three ablation arms required to validate the claim:
1. Same-task WM arm: parent MB vs redox-disabled analogue (N-acetyl or 10-N) — without this, Wen cannot bridge to WM.
2. MAO-A / selective MAO-A inhibitor contrast at matched MAO occupancy — without this, redox-dead fail does not kill 'MAO-explains-WM'.
3. Endpoint discipline (Wen ≠ WM) — without this, the analysis invents a WM result the seed overstated.

Refutation criterion: On the pre-registered WM task, if a redox-disabled MB analogue matches parent MB within the equivalence band, OR a selective MAO-A inhibitor at matched MAO occupancy reproduces parent MB WM within that band, then MAO-explains-WM survives.

content_blocks.title: Open Questions / Human Review Items
content_blocks.content: Lock WM task (delayed alternation vs holeboard vs object recognition), which redox-dead analogue (N-acetyl vs 10-N), and MAO occupancy readout before treating any MB cognitive signal as MAOI-like. Do not invent dosing. Peer-review requested. Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks. Kill cost tier: 1 (low cost).

key_findings: No existing study has performed a same-task working memory (WM) dissociation between MB's redox mechanism and MAO-A inhibition — this is the critical gap.

Wen 2011 (PMID 21454572) shows N-acetyl-MB (redox-disabled) loses mitochondrial complex activity, but this endpoint is neuroprotection/OCR, NOT working memory — the WM bridge is an inference by Gonzalez-Lima, not a direct result.
Poteet 2012 (PMID 23118969) shows 10-N side-chain substitution causes ~1000× drop in protective potency, supporting redox as the relevant mechanism for neuroprotection.
MB MAO-A IC50 ≈70 nM; Azure B MAO-A IC50 ≈11 nM (PMID 17721552; 22197611) — MAO-A potency is established but not linked to WM outcomes.

Low-dose MB improves discrimination learning and rescues PCC-metabolic amnesia with COX upregulation (Gonzalez-Lima class; PMID 17428524; 21087672) — memory benefit maps to metabolic/redox axis, not MAO.
Azure B metabolite confound: in vivo MB WM effects could still be mediated by metabolite MAO-A inhibition even if parent redox matters in vitro.

The proposed experiment is a pre-registered rodent WM task with two arms: (1) redox-disabled analogue vs parent MB, (2) selective MAO-A inhibitor at matched occupancy vs parent MB — neither arm has been executed.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill cost tier: 1 (low cost).
Document is classified as research-discussion / assumption-kill, not a completed experimental study — TRL 1 for the proposed dissociation assay.
